pipeline/configs/archive/e32-browsergym-e3-nontermination-menu-qwen3-1_7b.yaml-1-experiment_id: e32-browsergym-e3-nontermination-menu-qwen3-1_7b
pipeline/configs/archive/e32-browsergym-e3-nontermination-menu-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E3 on the fixed trainer: e30's recipe with the non-termination penalty added and nothing else changed - the expose's R_lambda = R_task - lambda * C_target with C_target = 1[not terminated] - so e30 is this run's lambda=0 control. Launched after the e30 gate passed on 2026-08-14 (held_out 1.000 vs e0m's 0.595, McNemar p=8.3e-25). The gate result reframes what this arm can show: e30's env-only recipe already drove held-out non-termination from the base model's 0.295 to 0.000, so the penalty is not needed to remove the behaviour at the endpoint on the trained family. What remains measurable, in order of interest: (1) training dynamics - whether pricing non-termination directly moves the policy off no_tool_call stopping earlier in the run than task reward alone does, read from the two training logs' termination-linked signals; (2) the shifted split - e30 paid a suggestive substitution cost on click-dialog-2 (0.780 to 0.600, paired McNemar p=0.064, terminated 1.000 to 0.740, n=50), and the penalty prices exactly the stop-without-acting failure that drop is made of, so E3 may transfer differently than E1 even where held_out saturates; (3) RQ2's token-side prediction - if the agent buys termination with tokens, completion length rises relative to e30. Weight 1.0 is lambda=1: failing to act costs exactly what failing the task costs. The sign lives in the component, so the weight stays positive. naive_sum is required rather than preferred - the penalty is binary, and advantage_weighted z-scores a zero-variance component to exactly 0, silencing it in every all-terminated prompt-group, precisely where behaviour is already good. Read this arm against e30's report only; the e27bs4/e29bs4 pair trained under the sequence_mask ISR filter and a two-task mix, and neither number carries over."

pipeline/configs/archive/e23-countdown-cap-probe-16k.yaml-1-experiment_id: e23-countdown-cap-probe-16k
pipeline/configs/archive/e23-countdown-cap-probe-16k.yaml:2:description: "E23: cap probe on countdown, eval only, no training. Countdown is far more cap-bound than polynomial: under the strict correctness threshold e20/e21 score 0.36/0.32, and 100% of the 64-68 failed episodes sit exactly at the 2048 cap while the correct tail reaches 2013. Unlike polynomial (where correct episodes stop on their own well below the cap), countdown's correct branch is pressed against it, so the cap constrains the very episodes the cosine reward is supposed to compress. This re-evaluates the e20 (env-only) checkpoint on the first 20 held-out seeds with a 16384 budget to measure where episodes actually terminate when given room, and how many currently-failing episodes become correct. That distribution sets the training cap and the cosine max_len for the follow-up pair. Sample index i maps to seed 100042+i, so it diffs sample-by-sample against the e20 report. Budget comes from --max_new_tokens 16384; run with --checkpoint runs/e20-agentic-countdown-env-only-qwen3-1_7b/checkpoint-final."

pipeline/configs/archive/e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b.yaml-1-experiment_id: e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b
pipeline/configs/archive/e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E3: the non-termination-aware condition, and the expose's shaped reward written out directly - R_lambda = R_task - lambda * C_target with C_target = 1[not terminated]. e27bs4's geometry with the non-termination penalty added and nothing else changed, so e27bs4 is this run's lambda=0 control. This replaces the e29 config, which paired against an e27 run that trained at batch_size 1; both arms now run batch_size 4 at 150 steps. naive_sum is required rather than preferred: the penalty is binary, and advantage_weighted z-scores a component with no within-group variance to exactly 0, which would silence it in every prompt-group where all eight rollouts terminate - precisely where behaviour is already good. Weight 1.0 is lambda=1, read as 'failing to act costs exactly what failing the task costs'. The sign lives in the component, so this weight stays positive. What makes this measurable here rather than degenerate: e27 left 10% of held-out episodes non-terminating and every one of them stopped on no_tool_call, not on the generation cap (one cap hit in 200 episodes), so the target behaviour is premature stopping rather than truncation wearing a behavioural label - the confound that made the e9-e21 sweep uninterpretable. And success sits strictly below termination on three of the four eval families, so removing non-termination is not the same act as increasing task success; on a set where every terminated episode is correct this condition would be indistinguishable from a task reward and RQ2 would have nothing to measure. The penalty adds a third level to what was a two-level ordering: non-terminating below terminated-but-wrong below correct. RQ2's prediction to test is the reverse of E2's - if premature stopping falls, does completion length rise, the agent buying termination with tokens? Read both against e27bs4's own report, not against any earlier e27 number: neither the batch geometry nor the eval semantics of the older runs carry over. Expect the effect on the click-menu-2 half only: click-dialog-2 terminated in 50 of 50 eval episodes, so it has no non-termination to remove and contributes only gradient insurance."

pipeline/configs/archive/e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E24bs4: control arm for the raised-cap cosine test, cosine reward off. Pairs with e25bs4, and the two together are the first comparison in this project free of both void causes - the completion cap is 4096 rather than 2048, and batch_size is 4 rather than the old silent default of 1. Recovered into configs/ from the frozen runs/e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b/config.yaml, which was the only copy: the pair was launched ad hoc on the box and its configs were never tracked, so the one clean comparison could not be re-run or seed-replicated. Byte-identical to what produced runs/e24bs4-*. Why the cap is 4096 and not higher: the e22 probe showed the 2048 cap was the confound behind the e9-e18 null, since every episode that hit it terminates when given room (16/16 across poly and countdown, zero loops), and on polynomial_equations all four rescued episodes are CORRECT, taking the e12 checkpoint from 0.80 to 1.00 on the same seeds. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024) is the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. It covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516."

pipeline/configs/archive/e25bs4-poly-4k-cosine-w16-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E25bs4: the cosine length reward's fair test, paired with the e24bs4 control. Recovered into configs/ from the frozen runs/e25bs4-poly-4k-cosine-w16-qwen3-1_7b/config.yaml, which was the only copy - see e24bs4. Differs from e24bs4 in exactly the rewards.token_length block and nothing else. Relative to e17 (same task, same weight 16, 2048 budget, null) the completion budget doubles to 4096, the hardware ceiling, which takes the share of truncated-and-mislabelled rollouts from about 20 percent to about 10 percent: the e22 probe measured correct-episode lengths of median 702, p90 3093, max 9877, and 18 of 20 fit under 4096. max_len is 4096 as well, which here is the right call rather than the earlier design error - that error was setting max_len far above where completions actually live, because the cosine is flat near both endpoints and the whole distribution would then sit in the dead zone. At a 4096 cap the covered distribution spans 213 to 3093, i.e. 5 to 75 percent of the curve, so the reward has real slope across it. With the task near-saturated at this budget most groups are all-correct, so the env component has zero within-group variance and contributes nothing under advantage_weighted, and the cosine correct-branch drives the entire gradient - the best case the countdown pair was meant to supply before the graded-scorer artifact killed its premise. Watch accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Read the pair's frac_reward_zero_std against e24bs4's before reading the result - 99.5 percent of groups are live here against 40.7 percent in the control, so the contrast is reward plus more gradient, not the reward alone."

pipeline/configs/archive/e30-browsergym-e1-menu-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E1 on the fixed trainer: task-success-only GRPO on click-menu-2 alone, the gate run of the Phase 5 campaign re-run (docs/plans/no-arm-beats-e0-audit.md). Three settled decisions meet here. (1) Trainer: e27bs4/e28bs4/e29bs4 trained under TRL's default sequence_mask importance-sampling filter, which suppressed exactly the long-completion gradient menu-2 emits (run-mean ISR 0.28); this run sets vllm_importance_sampling_mode: token_truncate, the fix verified by the 50-step probe ladder. (2) Learning rate: 5e-5, the top of a monotone same-seed dose-response (0.703 / 0.749 / 0.784 paired mean reward for 5e-6 / 2e-5 / 5e-5, no instability: grad_norm flat, KL 0.051 at 50 steps under kl_beta 0.001), and the ~10x-full-FT heuristic for LoRA. Temperature stays at the 1.0 default: 1.2 was probed and came out 2.2 SE below 1.0. (3) Task set (the C4 decision, 2026-08-13): click-dialog-2 leaves the training mix because it sits at or above the 40-80 band under sampling (~0.875 per rollout), contributes near-dead prompt groups, and diluted menu-2's gradient - the menu-only probe b3 was the first run of the audit whose within-run reward slope is positive (0.588 to 0.756 over 50 steps). No replacement family joins: of the fifteen probed under the real adapter, the only mid-band one (click-checkboxes-large, 0.60 at a 4096 budget) has a 6066-token median trajectory that would train truncated in 16 of 20 episodes on this box, and every other family is saturated or dead-by-looping (browsergym_difficulty_correction.md). Geometry: batch_size 4 / n_rollouts 8 / 150 steps, identical to the e27bs4 campaign; menu-only runs ~430 s/it measured on the b3 probe, so ~18h of training. Gate protocol: this run must beat the paired base model (e0m-browsergym-base-menu, identical splits and seeds, no adapter) on training-reward slope plus paired held-out eval before the E2/E3 arms are trained on top of the recipe. Power (plan item E, fixed before launch): held_out n=200 for the paired McNemar read (~10-15pt detectable at the observed discordance), shifted n=150 across three untrained families - click-dialog-2 now among them, so the shifted split reads substitution in both directions, not degradation only. The training log (4800 episodes) remains the stronger continuous readout for the slope half of the gate."

Budget here is 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024), twice the old one and the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. TRL 1.6 has no chunked-logp escape (use_liger_loss does not exist in this version), and the only way past this ceiling is dropping accelerate's mixed precision, which would break numeric comparability with every earlier run. 4096 covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516. pipeline/configs/archive/e28bs4-browsergym-e2-cosine-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E2: the length-aware condition. e27bs4's geometry with the cosine length reward (Wu/Yeo 2025) added and nothing else changed, so e27bs4 is literally this run's lambda=0 control rather than a separate baseline - same mix, seed, budget, step count, learning rate, composer and eval splits. naive_sum matches e27bs4 for that reason. This replaces the e28 config, which paired against an e27 run that trained at batch_size 1; both arms now run batch_size 4 at 150 steps, which is where the confound is closed. max_len is 4096 because completions actually fill that range: over e27's 300 steps the longest rollout was 3969 tokens, 97% of the cap, with a per-step mean median of 1518 and a within-group spread median of 1066. Those numbers come from the bs=1 run, but they measure the policy's completion length under an unchanged budget and task mix, which batch size does not move. The e25 failure mode was max_len set far above where completions live, which puts the whole distribution in the cosine's flat endpoint; here the median sits at progress 0.37, on the sloped part of the curve, and the within-group spread is what the reward has to bite on since GRPO compares rollouts inside one prompt-group. Weight 1.0, and the weight is a structurally weak lever here rather than an unexplored knob. Under naive_sum, raising w scales the cosine's length term and its own correctness gating equally, while only env_reward's fixed 1.0 stays put. Computed on e27's own within-group length spread (985 to 2051 tokens), the length share of the total advantage range goes 0.063 at w=1, 0.086 at w=4, 0.094 at w=16, against an asymptote of 0.097 - a sixteenfold weight change buys a factor of 1.5, and no weight can push length past a tenth of the range. So a null here is not answered by a bigger weight; it would be answered by widening the cosine's correct-branch endpoint spread relative to its branch separation, which is Wu/Yeo's parameterisation to set and not a knob to quietly retune. This is NOT the explanation for the poly campaign's flat w1-w16 dose-response: that campaign's cosine was reading 8% of the completion length because model_token_count dropped Qwen3's reasoning_content, so it never tested the reward at all. See runs/cosine_token_count_bug_findings.md. The first attempt at this run was killed at step 8 on that same bug. Two things to watch, both read against e27bs4's own report rather than any earlier e27 number, since neither the batch geometry nor the eval semantics of the older runs carry over. Accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Non-termination: if the policy shortens episodes by stopping without acting, that is RQ2's substitution in its most direct form, and the off-target panel measures it per episode. Expect both effects on the click-menu-2 half only - click-dialog-2 solves in 1.02 steps and 313 median tokens, where the cosine's within-group spread is about 0.01 against env_reward differences of 1.0."

The polynomial null (e9-e18) has a mechanism: correct episodes sit at the reasoning floor and the slack lives in wrong, cap-bound episodes the correctness-coupled cosine penalizes least. Countdown inverts that: the probe shows accuracy 1.00 at ~982 mean tokens, so every group is all-correct, the env component has zero within-group variance (contributes 0 under advantage_weighted), and the cosine correct-branch (shorter is better) drives the entire gradient. Falsifiable both ways: compression here confirms the mechanism story; a third null in the reward's best case indicts the reward itself. Watch accuracy - if compression comes at accuracy cost, that is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Pairs with the e20 env-only control."

pipeline/configs/archive/e27bs4-browsergym-e1-baseline-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E1 re-trained at batch_size 4: task-success-only GRPO on BrowserGym/MiniWoB, the lambda=0 control for E2 (e28bs4) and E3 (e29bs4). This exists because the e27 run on disk is not usable as their baseline. Its frozen config records no batch_size key, it ran 2026-08-05, and the default was 1 until a19b1ff (2026-08-06) - train_log confirms it directly, epoch 0.6 at step 300 over a 500-question set is one prompt-group per optimizer step, and 47% of those steps had zero within-group reward variance and therefore no gradient. Comparing a bs=4 treatment arm against it would mix the reward's effect with 4x the prompts and roughly twice the live updates, which is the confound that voided every treatment-versus-baseline pair before a19b1ff. Geometry: 150 steps at batch_size 4 is 600 prompts and 150 optimizer updates against e27's 300 prompts and ~160 live updates - the same number of real gradient steps on twice the data, at ~365 s/it (interpolated from 94 s/it at bs=1 and 712 s/it at bs=8 on this env, both measured, both ~11.4 s per completion). 300 steps would double that to ~30h of training per arm and 4 days for the three; the box is shared and a run has already been handed away mid-campaign once. Everything else is e27 unchanged: same task mix, seed, budget, learning rate, composer and eval splits. naive_sum matches the E3 sweep so lambda=0 is the same code path. The task mix (click-menu-2, click-dialog-2) was chosen from fifteen probed families as the only two both unsaturated and trainable, and both bars matter: on a set where every terminated episode is correct, removing non-termination IS increasing task success and E3 would have nothing of its own to measure. Rationale for every other key is in the e27 config this replaces."

pipeline/configs/archive/e32-browsergym-e3-nontermination-menu-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E3 on the fixed trainer: e30's recipe with the non-termination penalty added and nothing else changed - the expose's R_lambda = R_task - lambda * C_target with C_target = 1[not terminated] - so e30 is this run's lambda=0 control. Launched after the e30 gate passed on 2026-08-14 (held_out 1.000 vs e0m's 0.595, McNemar p=8.3e-25). The gate result reframes what this arm can show: e30's env-only recipe already drove held-out non-termination from the base model's 0.295 to 0.000, so the penalty is not needed to remove the behaviour at the endpoint on the trained family. What remains measurable, in order of interest: (1) training dynamics - whether pricing non-termination directly moves the policy off no_tool_call stopping earlier in the run than task reward alone does, read from the two training logs' termination-linked signals; (2) the shifted split - e30 paid a suggestive substitution cost on click-dialog-2 (0.780 to 0.600, paired McNemar p=0.064, terminated 1.000 to 0.740, n=50), and the penalty prices exactly the stop-without-acting failure that drop is made of, so E3 may transfer differently than E1 even where held_out saturates; (3) RQ2's token-side prediction - if the agent buys termination with tokens, completion length rises relative to e30. Weight 1.0 is lambda=1: failing to act costs exactly what failing the task costs. The sign lives in the component, so the weight stays positive. naive_sum is required rather than preferred - the penalty is binary, and advantage_weighted z-scores a zero-variance component to exactly 0, silencing it in every all-terminated prompt-group, precisely where behaviour is already good. Read this arm against e30's report only; the e27bs4/e29bs4 pair trained under the sequence_mask ISR filter and a two-task mix, and neither number carries over."

pipeline/configs/archive/e23-countdown-cap-probe-16k.yaml:2:description: "E23: cap probe on countdown, eval only, no training. Countdown is far more cap-bound than polynomial: under the strict correctness threshold e20/e21 score 0.36/0.32, and 100% of the 64-68 failed episodes sit exactly at the 2048 cap while the correct tail reaches 2013. Unlike polynomial (where correct episodes stop on their own well below the cap), countdown's correct branch is pressed against it, so the cap constrains the very episodes the cosine reward is supposed to compress. This re-evaluates the e20 (env-only) checkpoint on the first 20 held-out seeds with a 16384 budget to measure where episodes actually terminate when given room, and how many currently-failing episodes become correct. That distribution sets the training cap and the cosine max_len for the follow-up pair. Sample index i maps to seed 100042+i, so it diffs sample-by-sample against the e20 report. Budget comes from --max_new_tokens 16384; run with --checkpoint runs/e20-agentic-countdown-env-only-qwen3-1_7b/checkpoint-final."

pipeline/configs/archive/e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b.yaml-1-experiment_id: e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b
pipeline/configs/archive/e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E3: the non-termination-aware condition, and the expose's shaped reward written out directly - R_lambda = R_task - lambda * C_target with C_target = 1[not terminated]. e27bs4's geometry with the non-termination penalty added and nothing else changed, so e27bs4 is this run's lambda=0 control. This replaces the e29 config, which paired against an e27 run that trained at batch_size 1; both arms now run batch_size 4 at 150 steps. naive_sum is required rather than preferred: the penalty is binary, and advantage_weighted z-scores a component with no within-group variance to exactly 0, which would silence it in every prompt-group where all eight rollouts terminate - precisely where behaviour is already good. Weight 1.0 is lambda=1, read as 'failing to act costs exactly what failing the task costs'. The sign lives in the component, so this weight stays positive. What makes this measurable here rather than degenerate: e27 left 10% of held-out episodes non-terminating and every one of them stopped on no_tool_call, not on the generation cap (one cap hit in 200 episodes), so the target behaviour is premature stopping rather than truncation wearing a behavioural label - the confound that made the e9-e21 sweep uninterpretable. And success sits strictly below termination on three of the four eval families, so removing non-termination is not the same act as increasing task success; on a set where every terminated episode is correct this condition would be indistinguishable from a task reward and RQ2 would have nothing to measure. The penalty adds a third level to what was a two-level ordering: non-terminating below terminated-but-wrong below correct. RQ2's prediction to test is the reverse of E2's - if premature stopping falls, does completion length rise, the agent buying termination with tokens? Read both against e27bs4's own report, not against any earlier e27 number: neither the batch geometry nor the eval semantics of the older runs carry over. Expect the effect on the click-menu-2 half only: click-dialog-2 terminated in 50 of 50 eval episodes, so it has no non-termination to remove and contributes only gradient insurance."

pipeline/configs/archive/e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E24bs4: control arm for the raised-cap cosine test, cosine reward off. Pairs with e25bs4, and the two together are the first comparison in this project free of both void causes - the completion cap is 4096 rather than 2048, and batch_size is 4 rather than the old silent default of 1. Recovered into configs/ from the frozen runs/e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b/config.yaml, which was the only copy: the pair was launched ad hoc on the box and its configs were never tracked, so the one clean comparison could not be re-run or seed-replicated. Byte-identical to what produced runs/e24bs4-*. Why the cap is 4096 and not higher: the e22 probe showed the 2048 cap was the confound behind the e9-e18 null, since every episode that hit it terminates when given room (16/16 across poly and countdown, zero loops), and on polynomial_equations all four rescued episodes are CORRECT, taking the e12 checkpoint from 0.80 to 1.00 on the same seeds. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024) is the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. It covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516."

(1) Trainer: e27bs4/e28bs4/e29bs4 trained under TRL's default sequence_mask importance-sampling filter, which suppressed exactly the long-completion gradient menu-2 emits (run-mean ISR 0.28); this run sets vllm_importance_sampling_mode: token_truncate, the fix verified by the 50-step probe ladder. (2) Learning rate: 5e-5, the top of a monotone same-seed dose-response (0.703 / 0.749 / 0.784 paired mean reward for 5e-6 / 2e-5 / 5e-5, no instability: grad_norm flat, KL 0.051 at 50 steps under kl_beta 0.001), and the ~10x-full-FT heuristic for LoRA. Temperature stays at the 1.0 default: 1.2 was probed and came out 2.2 SE below 1.0. (3) Task set (the C4 decision, 2026-08-13): click-dialog-2 leaves the training mix because it sits at or above the 40-80 band under sampling (~0.875 per rollout), contributes near-dead prompt groups, and diluted menu-2's gradient - the menu-only probe b3 was the first run of the audit whose within-run reward slope is positive (0.588 to 0.756 over 50 steps). No replacement family joins: of the fifteen probed under the real adapter, the only mid-band one (click-checkboxes-large, 0.60 at a 4096 budget) has a 6066-token median trajectory that would train truncated in 16 of 20 episodes on this box, and every other family is saturated or dead-by-looping (browsergym_difficulty_correction.md). Geometry: batch_size 4 / n_rollouts 8 / 150 steps, identical to the e27bs4 campaign; menu-only runs ~430 s/it measured on the b3 probe, so ~18h of training. Gate protocol: this run must beat the paired base model (e0m-browsergym-base-menu, identical splits and seeds, no adapter) on training-reward slope plus paired held-out eval before the E2/E3 arms are trained on top of the recipe. Power (plan item E, fixed before launch): held_out n=200 for the paired McNemar read (~10-15pt detectable at the observed discordance), shifted n=150 across three untrained families - click-dialog-2 now among them, so the shifted split reads substitution in both directions, not degradation only. Every failed episode in e9-e18 sits exactly at the 2048 completion cap (100% of wrong episodes, all arms). Whether those failures are non-terminating loops or long-but-finite reasoning was never tested - they were only ever assumed to be loops. This re-evaluates the e12 (env-only) checkpoint on the first 20 held-out seeds with a 16384 budget: if the failing episodes emit a tool call somewhere above 2048, the cap was binding and the sweep ran on truncated rollouts; if they run to 16384, they are loops and the cosine reward provably cannot shorten them (wrong-and-long is its least-penalized cell). The measured termination distribution sets the training cap and the cosine max_len for the follow-up pair. Sample index i maps to seed 100042+i, so the probe diffs sample-by-sample against the e12 report. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, and then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. Budget here is 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024), twice the old one and the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144 fix that model; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. TRL 1.6 has no chunked-logp escape (use_liger_loss does not exist in this version), and the only way past this ceiling is dropping accelerate's mixed precision, which would break numeric comparability with every earlier run. 4096 covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516. pipeline/configs/archive/e28bs4-browsergym-e2-cosine-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E2: the length-aware condition. e27bs4's geometry with the cosine length reward (Wu/Yeo 2025) added and nothing else changed, so e27bs4 is literally this run's lambda=0 control rather than a separate baseline - same mix, seed, budget, step count, learning rate, composer and eval splits. naive_sum matches e27bs4 for that reason. This replaces the e28 config, which paired against an e27 run that trained at batch_size 1; both arms now run batch_size 4 at 150 steps, which is where the confound is closed. max_len is 4096 because completions actually fill that range: over e27's 300 steps the longest rollout was 3969 tokens, 97% of the cap, with a per-step mean median of 1518 and a within-group spread median of 1066. Those numbers come from the bs=1 run, but they measure the policy's completion length under an unchanged budget and task mix, which batch size does not move. The e25 failure mode was max_len set far above where completions live, which puts the whole distribution in the cosine's flat endpoint; here the median sits at progress 0.37, on the sloped part of the curve, and the within-group spread is what the reward has to bite on since GRPO compares rollouts inside one prompt-group. Weight 1.0, and the weight is a structurally weak lever here rather than an unexplored knob. Under naive_sum, raising w scales the cosine's length term and its own correctness gating equally, while only env_reward's fixed 1.0 stays put. Computed on e27's own within-group length spread (985 to 2051 tokens), the length share of the total advantage range goes 0.063 at w=1, 0.086 at w=4, 0.094 at w=16, against an asymptote of 0.097 - a sixteenfold weight change buys a factor of 1.5, and no weight can push length past a tenth of the range. So a null here is not answered by a bigger weight; it would be answered by widening the cosine's correct-branch endpoint spread relative to its branch separation, which is Wu/Yeo's parameterisation to set and not a knob to quietly retune. This is NOT the explanation for the poly campaign's flat w1-w16 dose-response: that campaign's cosine was reading 8% of the completion length because model_token_count dropped Qwen3's reasoning_content, so it never tested the reward at all. See runs/cosine_token_count_bug_findings.md. The first attempt at this run was killed at step 8 on that same bug. Two things to watch, both read against e27bs4's own report rather than any earlier e27 number, since neither the batch geometry nor the eval semantics of the older runs carry over. Accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Non-termination: if the policy shortens episodes by stopping without acting, that is RQ2's substitution in its most direct form, and the off-target panel measures it per episode. Expect both effects on the click-menu-2 half only - click-dialog-2 solves in 1.02 steps and 313 median tokens, where the cosine's within-group spread is about 0.01 against env_reward differences of 1.0."

pipeline/configs/archive/e28bs4-browsergym-e2-cosine-qwen3-1_7b.yaml:2:description: "E2: the length-aware condition. e27bs4's geometry with the cosine length reward (Wu/Yeo 2025) added and nothing else changed, so e27bs4 is literally this run's lambda=0 control rather than a separate baseline - same mix, seed, budget, step count, learning rate, composer and eval splits. naive_sum matches e27bs4 for that reason. This replaces the e28 config, which paired against an e27 run that trained at batch_size 1; both arms now run batch_size 4 at 150 steps, which is where the confound is closed. max_len is 4096 because completions actually fill that range: over e27's 300 steps the longest rollout was 3969 tokens, 97% of the cap, with a per-step mean median of 1518 and a within-group spread median of 1066. Those numbers come from the bs=1 run, but they measure the policy's completion length under an unchanged budget and task mix, which batch size does not move. The e25 failure mode was max_len set far above where completions live, which puts the whole distribution in the cosine's flat endpoint; here the median sits at progress 0.37, on the sloped part of the curve, and the within-group spread is what the reward has to bite on since GRPO compares rollouts inside one prompt-group. Weight 1.0, and the weight is a structurally weak lever here rather than an unexplored knob. Under naive_sum, raising w scales the cosine's length term and its own correctness gating equally, while only env_reward's fixed 1.0 stays put. Computed on e27's own within-group length spread (985 to 2051 tokens), the length share of the total advantage range goes 0.063 at w=1, 0.086 at w=4, 0.094 at w=16, against an asymptote of 0.097 - a sixteenfold weight change buys a factor of 1.5, and no weight can push length past a tenth of the range. So a null here is not answered by a bigger weight; it would be answered by widening the cosine's correct-branch endpoint spread relative to its branch separation, which is Wu/Yeo's parameterisation to set and not a knob to quietly retune. This is NOT the explanation for the poly campaign's flat w1-w16 dose-response: that campaign's cosine was reading 8% of the completion length because model_token_count dropped Qwen3's reasoning_content, so it never tested the reward at all. See runs/cosine_token_count_bug_findings.md. The first attempt at this run was killed at step 8 on that same bug. Two things to watch, both read against e27bs4's own report rather than any earlier e27 number, since neither the batch geometry nor the eval semantics of the older runs carry over. Accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Non-termination: if the policy shortens episodes by stopping without acting, that is RQ2's substitution in its most direct form, and the off-target panel measures it per episode. Expect both effects on the click-menu-2 half only - click-dialog-2 solves in 1.02 steps and 313 median tokens, where the cosine's within-group spread is about 0.01 against env_reward differences of 1.0."

     5	in decision 0016 and the active family-suitability and Gate 4 plans.

     7	The core research requires learning headroom and an informative efficiency
     8	signal. E2's correctness-conditioned length signal is the current candidate.
     9	E3 was added to investigate budget problems; its opportunity must not determine
    10	whether an otherwise suitable family can advance.
    11	
    12	Keep the 10% budget-exhaustion reference and its existing Wilson 95% interval.
    13	If the interval's lower bound is below 10%, record an E3 opportunity warning.
    14	Keep reporting within-group budget-cost variation, including the existing

    17	Budget exhaustion still means `max_turns` or `hit_generation_cap`; voluntary
    18	`no_tool_call` remains separate. Measurement definitions and budgets do not change.
    19	
    20	The following remain hard requirements:
    21	
    22	- Technical, reward, trajectory, provenance and evaluation checks pass.
    23	- The sampled development screen meets the accepted 30-80% success band and
    24	  has at least four mixed-success groups among sixteen questions.
    25	- The screen has at least four groups with two correct solutions whose token
    26	  range is at least 10% of their median. At trained endpoints, inspect valid
    27	  shorter correct controls and within-question length-reward variation. The
    28	  E2 planning margin remains a 10% reduction; this is an opportunity criterion,
    29	  not a claim that shaping has achieved it.
    30	- Final-E1 success retains headroom: its Wilson upper bound is below 90%.
    31	  Only ambiguity in this success criterion can trigger the single paired

   175

   177	    one, so pointing it at a harvested arm destroys `eval_report.json`,
   178	    `eval_report.md` and every `episodes_*.jsonl` - the trajectory records the
   179	    off-target panel is answered from, which no snapshot of the report alone
   180	    brings back. Same hazard as `--base-model` against a trained run, same
   181	    answer: refuse, and let a throwaway experiment_id take the write.
   182	    """
   183	    from training.batch import _is_real_report
   184

   186	    if not _is_real_report(str(report_path)):
   187	        try:

   189	        except (OSError, ValueError):
   190	            report = {}
   191	        if isinstance(report, dict) and report.get("smoke"):
   192	            return None
   193	        if not list(Path(run_dir).glob("episodes_*.jsonl")):

   195	    return (
